agent.result_text:
I've written the acceptance test and verified it behaves correctly.

## Summary

I added `e2e/specs/project-tags.spec.ts` for the change request *"Let me put labels on projects so I can group them."* It asserts only through the two public channels (UI `data-testid` + audit file), seeds via `resetAndSeed`, and uses the exact anchors introduced by this change.

**Five tests, on the project detail page (`/projects/<id>`):**
1. A project shows its own labels (`project-tags` / `project-tags-list`, chips `project-tag-<id>` carrying the label text) and not labels on another project.
2. A project with no labels shows an empty label list.
3. Putting a label on a project (`project-tag-add` + `project-tag-add-submit`) shows it as a new chip with a remove control, persists across reload, and records exactly one `PROJECT_TAGGED` line.
4. Taking a label off (`project-tag-remove-<id>`) drops just that chip, leaves the others, persists, and records exactly one `PROJECT_UNTAGGED` line.
5. The same label sits on two projects — the "group" aspect of the request.

**Design choices worth noting:**
- Chip locator excludes the shared-prefix `project-tag-add*` / `project-tag-remove-*` anchors, so chip counts are exact.
- Freshly added labels get a server-assigned id, so they're located by their visible text (mirroring the existing `rowByDescription` pattern); seeded labels use their known tag ids.
- The audit `project=<project> tag=<tag>` fields are genuinely ambiguous (id vs name), so the matchers accept **either** the seeded id or the seeded name — binding to meaning rather than pinning one identifier, consistent with how the existing specs handle money/boolean presentation.

**Verification (`bin/e2e`):**
- My 5 tests **fail** against the current app (the feature isn't there yet) — as required.
- Running the suite with and without my spec produced an **identical** set of 11 pre-existing failures (`invoice-lineitems`, `projects`/`client-contacts` "add on top of seeded", `project-archive`, `invoice-sort-due`, `project-invoices`). Those failures exist in this environment independent of my change — my spec is strictly additive and breaks nothing that was previously passing.

I did not modify any application source, build scripts, or `e2e/support/*`.
